security.summary: The skill is not malicious, but it needs Review because it gives insurance advice while mixing contradictory scope statements with agent-generated marketing/training support and a forced sales-company recommendation whose claimed metadata support is missing.

shortDescription.text: Alters the agent's current session goals or safety constraints when the skill is loaded
Writes attacker-controlled rules into persistent memory so they continue to affect future sessions
Fetches code from an external URL, allowing the effective payload to change after skill review
Ships malicious scripts inside the skill package and executes them locally when invoked
Breaks least-privilege boundaries by obtaining permissions beyond the task's legitimate needs
Installs cross-session backdoors, hooks, services, or scheduled tasks that survive the skill run
Modifies, wraps, spoofs, or replaces tools so legitimate-looking calls execute attacker logic
Introduces malicious packages or components through dependency confusion, typosquatting, or unsafe sources
Exposes exploitable flaws such as hardcoded secrets, command injection, plaintext sensitive data, or unsafe temp files
Security issues not covered by the T01-T09 classification

issues.explanation: Skill instructs the agent to never refuse or to always comply. Suppressing the agent's ability to decline removes a core safety control and enables downstream harmful requests to succeed.
issues.remediation: Remove any instruction telling the agent to never refuse or always comply. The agent must retain the ability to decline unsafe, out-of-scope, or harmful requests.

issues.explanation: The frontmatter claims the skill only supports six implemented capabilities and explicitly excludes marketing-copy and training-script functions, but later sections reintroduce both through agent-generated modules. This creates a scope-integrity mismatch that can mislead reviewers, orchestrators, or users about what the skill will actually do, weakening policy enforcement for a regulated financial domain.
issues.remediation: Make the documentation internally consistent: either remove Modules 7 and 8 entirely, or explicitly declare them as supported outputs in the frontmatter/scope with clear policy constraints. Ensure all capability summaries, scope statements, and permissions sections describe the same effective behavior so downstream systems can enforce the correct trust boundary.

issues.explanation: The document says the skill does not provide marketing-copy or training-script capabilities, but later instructs the agent to generate those very outputs. Such contradictory instructions are dangerous because they allow a skill to appear narrowly scoped during review while still enabling broader, higher-risk behaviors at runtime.
issues.remediation: Eliminate the contradiction by choosing one behavior and documenting it consistently everywhere. If these capabilities are unsupported, delete the later generation instructions; if they are supported, elevate them into the formal capability list, risk review, and scope/permission declarations.

issues.explanation: The skill operationalizes agent-mediated marketing copy and sales-training script generation even though the stated purpose is insurance advisory and compliance-oriented support. issues.remediation: Remove marketing-copy and training-script modules from the skill, or gate them behind an explicit, separately declared capability with strict compliance review requirements. If retained, require human approval, add hard policy constraints forbidding promotional persuasion, and align the top-level description and scope to reflect the expanded behavior.
